---
title: "Appendix · Using your own data"
subtitle: "Everything that changes when you point the workflow at real reads — plus fixes for the usual snags."
---

You've run the whole workflow on a toy. Here's everything that changes when you point
it at real reads — plus the fixes for the snags people usually hit.

## 1 · Use the *real* human index

This is the one non-negotiable swap. The `toy_human` index that shipped with the
repo is only the human **mitochondrion** — a stand-in so Step 1 runs in seconds. It
removes almost no host DNA.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Never run the toy index on real data
It will silently pass through the vast majority of human reads — into your results
and, worse, into any files you archive. On real samples, always dehost against the
**full human genome**.
:::

Build a real host index once, then reuse it forever. Grab a decoy-aware human
reference (T2T-CHM13 or GRCh38) and index it with the *same* `bowtie2-build` VANISH
uses:

```bash
# ~3 GB download; the index build takes a while and needs ~16 GB RAM
wget -O GRCh38.fa.gz \
  https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-110/fasta/homo_sapiens/dna/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna.primary_assembly.fa.gz
gunzip GRCh38.fa.gz

bowtie2-build --threads 8 GRCh38.fa human_GRCh38
```

Then point VANISH at it instead of the toy — everything else in
[Step 1](vanish.qmd) is identical:

```bash
vanish --read_pairs read_pairs.csv \
       --fastq_dir /path/to/your/reads \
       --host_index human_GRCh38 \
       --cpus 8
```

Now the `vanish_filtering_report.csv` will show host removal doing real work.

## 2 · Bring your own reads

Two small things change for your own samples:

- **Mate naming.** Tell `vanish-prep` how *your* files name their mates. Ours were
  `_1` / `_2`; yours might be `_R1` / `_R2`:
  ```bash
  vanish-prep --fastq_dir /path/to/your/reads --r1 "_R1" --r2 "_R2" --out read_pairs.csv
  ```
- **Multiple runs per sample.** If a sample was sequenced more than once, list *all*
  its reads on one samplesheet line — mates joined by commas, runs separated by
  semicolons:
  ```default
  SAMPLE_A,runX_R1.fq.gz,runX_R2.fq.gz;runY_R1.fq.gz,runY_R2.fq.gz
  ```
  Pooling every run per sample is what makes the **lateral coverage** metric honest
  (see [Step 2](resscan.qmd)).

Everything downstream — `resscan_batch`, `resscan_aggregate`, the whole
[analysis](analysis.qmd) — is unchanged. Same commands, your data.

## 3 · Keep the database current

CARD is updated regularly. To rebuild against a newer release, download it from
[card.mcmaster.ca](https://card.mcmaster.ca/) and rebuild — same two steps as in
Setup, just a new version string:

```bash
resscan_build_db -i CARD_raw -d resscan_CARD_v4.x.y
```

Record which CARD version you used with your results — resistome numbers aren't
comparable across database versions.

## 4 · Scale, cost, and cleanup

- **Threads vs. parallel.** In `resscan_batch`, `--parallel` is how many samples run
  at once and `--threads` is cores per sample. Total cores used ≈ `parallel × threads`
  — set both to fit your machine, not beyond it.
- **Disk.** Nextflow's `work/` directory grows fast and outlives the run. Delete it
  once you have the results you want:
  ```bash
  rm -rf work .nextflow*
  ```
- **Environments.** `mamba deactivate` when you're done, and remove an env entirely
  with `mamba env remove -n vanish-env` (or `resscan-env`).

## 5 · Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause & fix |
|---|---|
| `command not found: vanish` / `resscan` | The environment isn't active — `mamba activate vanish-env` (or `resscan-env`). |
| `environment.yml … pip install .` fails | You must be **inside** the cloned repo when creating the env: `( cd tools/vanish && mamba env create -f environment.yml )`. |
| VANISH removes ~0 host reads | You're on the **toy** index. Build and use the real human index (§1). |
| `ERROR: Samplesheet '…' not found` | Path is relative to where you launched. Run from the repo root, or pass an absolute path. |
| `Duplicate Sample IDs detected` | Two rows share a `sample_id`. If it's the same sample across runs, merge them onto **one** line with `;`. |
| Per-sample ResScan tables are empty | Expected on the 10K subset — too shallow. Depth, not a bug (see [Step 2](resscan.qmd)). |
| Nextflow `work/` filled the disk | `rm -rf work .nextflow*` after each successful run. |
| Analysis fold-changes look wrong / miss known genes | Aggregate **per sample first, then average** — don't `mean()` over raw gene×sample cells (see [Step 3](analysis.qmd)). |

That's the whole workflow, toy to real. Clean reads in, calibrated per-cell numbers
out, a resistome you can actually reason about.
